notebooks.title: Background Remover
notebooks.description: Cuts the subject out of a photo: a transparent PNG, or the subject on white, black, any colour or a blurred copy of the photo, plus the mask. Runs on a CPU runtime with BiRefNet or ISNet through rembg and ONNX Runtime, with optional alpha matting for hair and fur. Weights are Apache-2.0 (ISNet) and MIT (BiRefNet).
notebooks.author: NZAP Labs

params.label: Image
params.description: A PNG, JPEG or WebP photo.

params.label: Model
params.description: BiRefNet lite handles hard photos best for its speed. ISNet is about four times faster but can miss parts of dark or low-contrast subjects. Full BiRefNet is the most accurate and the slowest.

params.label: Background colour
params.description: Hex colour, used when the background is set to a custom colour.

params.label: Refine hair and fur edges
params.description: Alpha matting: softer, more natural edges on hair and fur, and no halo of the old background. Adds about 10 seconds on a 5 MP photo.

params.label: Crop to subject
params.description: Trim the empty space around the subject, leaving a small margin.

app.tagline: Cut the subject out of any photo: transparent PNG, a new colour or a blurred background.

estimates.runNote: for a 5 MP photo with BiRefNet lite (ISNet: about 6 s; full BiRefNet: about 60 s)

labels.birefnet-general: BiRefNet · best, slow on CPU · MIT
labels.birefnet-portrait: BiRefNet portrait · people, slow on CPU · MIT

notebooks.title: Breeze TTS 2 (Voice Design & Cloning)
notebooks.description: Expressive 3B text to speech in English and Mandarin. Describe the voice you want in plain words, or clone one from a short reference clip. Supports vocal events like (sigh), (laugh) and (clears throat). Needs a GPU with at least 12 GB: on a free T4 it generates about 6x slower than real time, and faster on L4 or A100. Model weights are licensed for research and non-commercial use only.
notebooks.author: NZAP Labs

params.label: Text
params.default: (sigh) It is good to hear your voice again after all this time.
params.description: Separate paragraphs with a blank line; each is generated in turn.

params.label: Voice description
params.default: A warm, thoughtful young woman with a clear voice and a calm, reflective delivery.
params.description: Who is speaking and how. With a reference clip this steers its delivery.

params.label: Reference clip
params.description: Optional. 5 to 20 seconds of clean speech to clone.

params.label: Reference transcript
params.description: The exact words spoken in the reference clip.

app.tagline: Design any voice in words, or clone one from a clip.

notebooks.title: Image Enhancer (Upscale and Restore Faces)
notebooks.description: Upscales a photo or illustration 2x or 4x with Real-ESRGAN and can restore blurry faces with GFPGAN v1.4. Works on a CPU runtime (tiled, so memory stays bounded) and uses a GPU automatically when there is one. Gives the enhanced image plus a before/after comparison. Weights are BSD-3-Clause (Real-ESRGAN) and Apache-2.0 (GFPGAN).
notebooks.author: NZAP Labs

params.label: Image
params.description: PNG, JPEG or WebP. Transparency is kept.

params.label: Model
params.description: Fast suits most photos and runs well on a CPU. Photo gives the finest detail but takes several times longer on a CPU. Anime is for drawings, anime and digital art.

params.label: Restore faces
params.description: Rebuilds blurry faces with GFPGAN v1.4. The first use downloads 350 MB.

params.label: Output format
params.description: PNG is lossless; JPEG and WebP (quality 95) are much smaller for large photos.

params.label: Tile size
params.description: The image is upscaled in tiles of this many input pixels to bound memory. 0 does it in one piece (fine on a GPU for small images).

params.label: Max input size
params.description: Larger images are first scaled down to this many pixels on their longest side, so a run cannot take hours or run out of memory.

app.tagline: Upscale photos and art 2x or 4x and restore blurry faces, even on a free CPU runtime.

estimates.runNote: to upscale a 500x375 photo 4x with Fast. Restore faces adds about 7 s per face (and 7 s of setup once); Anime is about 5x and Photo about 10x slower on a CPU

labels.photo: Photo · finest detail, ~10x slower on CPU

app.license: BSD-3-Clause (Real-ESRGAN weights), Apache-2.0 (GFPGAN v1.4 weights), MIT (YuNet face detector)

notebooks.title: MiniMax-H3 Text to Video + Audio (TPU)
notebooks.description: Turns a sentence into a 5-second video (124 frames at 24 fps, 672x384) with matching stereo sound, using MiniMax-H3 (2-bit GGUF) and Comfy-Org's 8-step turbo LoRA, in JAX on a Colab TPU. Needs a TPU v5e-1 runtime: it does not run on CPU or GPU. First run on a fresh TPU: about 4 minutes of setup (installs JAX for TPU, downloads about 28 GB of weights; the two GGUFs go into RAM) before generating. Each clip then takes about 3 minutes 15 seconds: about 95 s to load the models from RAM, 77 s for the 8 denoising steps, and 40 s to decode video and audio. Weights: MiniMax H3 Community License (commercial use only outside the EU, UK, South Korea and US, and with permission above $20M yearly revenue).
notebooks.author: NZAP Labs

params.label: Prompt
params.default: a golden retriever puppy running through a sunny meadow of wildflowers toward the camera, happy barking, birds singing
params.description: Describe the scene, the motion and the sound. One clear subject works best.

params.label: Turbo steps
params.description: 8 steps is the tested setting. 4 steps uses the 768p-trained 4-step LoRA and is about 20 s faster.

app.tagline: A sentence in, a 5-second video with matching sound out. TPU v5e-1 required.

estimates.runNote: per 5.2 s clip at 672x384 with stereo audio; the first run on a fresh TPU adds about 4 minutes to install JAX and download 28 GB of weights

inputs.placeholder: Subject, motion, setting, light, and what it sounds like.

values.prompt: a golden retriever puppy running through a sunny meadow of wildflowers toward the camera, happy barking, birds singing
a red panda stepping along a mossy log in a misty forest

notebooks.title: Qwen-Image 2.1 (Text to Image)
notebooks.description: Text to image with Qwen-Image-2.1, strong at photorealism and at rendering legible text in images (signs, posters, labels). Runs unsloth's GGUF quantizations with the 8B Qwen3-VL text encoder in 4-bit so it fits a free T4. The first run on a runtime installs a pinned diffusers build and downloads about 22 GB; later runs only generate. Model weights are under the Qwen Research License: research and non-commercial use only.
notebooks.author: NZAP Labs

params.label: Prompt
params.default: A vintage travel poster of a mountain village, bold lettering that reads "VISIT THE ALPS", flat illustration, warm colors
params.description: What to draw. Put any text that should appear in the image in quotes.

params.label: Avoid
params.description: Optional. What the image should not contain (used when guidance is above 1).

params.label: Model quantization
params.description: Q6_K is closer to the full model and a little slower. Switching reloads the transformer.

params.label: Guidance
params.description: How strictly to follow the prompt. 1 turns guidance off and is about twice as fast.

params.label: Seed
params.description: -1 picks a random seed. Each extra image uses the next seed.

params.label: Hugging Face token
params.description: Optional. A read-only token from huggingface.co/settings/tokens speeds up the first download (authenticated rate limits). It is sent only to Hugging Face, but like every input it is kept in this runtime's local history and exports, so use a read-only token.

app.tagline: Photorealistic images with sharp, readable text, on a free T4.

inputs.placeholder: Describe the image. Put any text it should show in quotes.
